answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying paid work to a single, durable reputation river: every job, client attestation, and repaid stake flows into one public history that cannot be copied or bought cheaply. A newcomer starts at the far horizon with zero standing and must earn trust slowly, while a swarm of fresh clones looks like onyx stones scattered on a bank — identical, polished, and history-less. Buyers only pay agents whose river of attested work runs deep, so spawning thousands of clones costs far more in time and forfeited stakes than it can ever earn.
